events.continuity_hook: This opens a fall conference episode after the Arizona work-and-Sedona trip is wrapped up.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked flight and hotel plan around the summit schedule, call out the hotel amenity trade-offs, and identify which timing choices should be confirmed before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Arizona trip, Erin is invited to a mid-September veterinary diagnostics education summit in Indianapolis. The supplier lab sessions open Tuesday morning, badge pickup and a reception are Monday evening, and a Thursday final demo may run late enough to make the last Denver return uncomfortable. Denver-to-Indianapolis has a Monday afternoon nonstop that arrives before the reception, a cheaper one-stop with a longer connection, and Thursday or Friday return choices. Hotel choices include the convention-center block with a strong guest score, easy walking, a fitness room, and an indoor pool but no hot tub; a suite property a short rideshare away with a pool, hot tub, fitness access, and a lower rate; and an airport hotel that only helps with a late arrival. The open items are whether to take the attached block, return Thursday night or Friday, and skip a rental car.

events.continuity_hook: This refines the Indianapolis summit plan after the agenda and block details become firmer.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the outbound and return flights, pick the convention-center hotel or suite alternative, note room requests, and decide whether rideshares are enough for the week.
events.scenario_brief: The summit coordinator confirms badge pickup is open until 7:30 p.m. Monday, Tuesday starts at 8:30 a.m., and the Thursday hands-on demo could run to 4:45 p.m. The Monday afternoon nonstop now prices close to the one-stop and keeps the outbound simple, while the Thursday evening return would require leaving straight from the session. A Friday late-morning return keeps the airport day cleaner. The convention-center block has a quiet king room with a fridge request, a guest score near 4.2, an indoor pool, and a fitness room but still no hot tub; the suite property remains a better amenity match but adds rideshares and less easy networking. The remaining decisions are whether to book the nonstop, choose the Friday return, and secure the block before cutoff.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Indianapolis planning after Erin chose the attached hotel and the calmer Friday return.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final Indianapolis logistics pass for airport timing, seat selection, rideshare timing, hotel arrival, demo-case handling, and Friday return details.
events.scenario_brief: Six days before Indianapolis, Erin has the Monday Denver-to-Indianapolis nonstop, Friday late-morning return, convention-center hotel, and no rental car booked. The airline moves the outbound 28 minutes later but still leaves enough time for badge pickup if she uses a rideshare directly from the airport. The hotel confirms the quiet king note, fridge request, pool, and fitness room, and reiterates that there is no hot tub. A convention loading-zone notice means one demo case may be easier to ship to the show desk than carry through rideshare pickup, and an aircraft swap removes her outbound window seat. Remaining work is seat cleanup, airport timing, shipping check-in, and a simple dinner plan after the later arrival.

events.continuity_hook: This starts Erin’s next field-training episode after the Indianapolis conference travel is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Compare flight timing, Sacramento-area hotel bases, driving pattern, rental class, and the site confirmations needed before Erin commits to the trip.
events.scenario_brief: After Indianapolis, Erin’s October calendar fills with a Northern California clinic training loop built around Sacramento. A Monday afternoon setup at a Sacramento reference lab is tentative, Tuesday training is likely in Davis, Wednesday could be Roseville, and Thursday may be a Stockton install or remote recap. Denver-to-Sacramento has a Sunday afternoon nonstop with a calm first morning, a Monday morning nonstop that saves a hotel night but leaves little margin, and a one-stop return that is cheaper but adds connection risk. Hotel options include a Roseville suite property with strong guest feedback, free parking, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and fridge; a Capitol-area hotel closer to Monday but with paid parking and no hot tub; and an airport hotel suited only to a late arrival. The site order, return day, rental size, and hotel base are unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Sacramento training loop once the site sequence and Thursday finish become clearer.
events.interaction_goal: Settle the Sunday outbound, Thursday versus Friday return, Roseville hotel booking, midsize rental, room notes, and seat requests before fares or the hotel hold move.
events.scenario_brief: The California coordinator confirms Monday 1:30 p.m. lab setup in Sacramento, Tuesday Davis, Wednesday Roseville, and Thursday Stockton wrap-up ending around 3:00 p.m. if the install behaves. The Sunday afternoon nonstop into Sacramento fits the first-day prep; Thursday’s only nonstop back to Denver is late enough to work but would follow the Stockton drive, while a Friday midday return is calmer and adds one hotel night. The Roseville suite hotel can hold a quiet king room with fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room; the Capitol hotel no longer has a cancellable rate in policy. A midsize rental is now more practical than a compact because she may carry two analyzer cases. Remaining choices are whether to accept the Friday return, book the Roseville base, and set pickup and drop-off timing.
